sections.h2: Where is Fredericksburg, Virginia, and how is it laid out?
sections.html:
Fredericksburg is a compact independent city of about 10.5 square miles on the Rappahannock River, roughly 53 miles south of downtown Washington, D.C. The river forms its northern and eastern edge, with Stafford County across the water, and Spotsylvania County wraps the south and west.

The city sits on the fall line, the boundary between the Piedmont and Tidewater regions, at an elevation of about 59 feet. Interstate 95, U.S. 1 and U.S. 17 all pass through, and Route 3 runs west toward the large shopping centers and on toward Culpeper. The Census Bureau counted 27,982 residents in 2020 and estimates 30,393 for 2025.

Fredericksburg became an independent city in 1879, so no county sits between the city and the state. The city bills its own real estate tax, and a house across a boundary street in Spotsylvania or Stafford is taxed by a different government.

sections.h2: What is Fredericksburg's history, and why does it matter to a house?
sections.html:
Fredericksburg was founded in 1728, incorporated as a town in 1781, and grew as a colonial port at the head of navigation on the Rappahannock. It stood halfway between the Union and Confederate capitals during the Civil War and was the site of the Battle of Fredericksburg in 1862. Parts of the battlefields are preserved in the Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park, which Congress formed in 1927.

The 40-block Fredericksburg Historic District was listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1971 and holds more than 350 buildings from the 18th and 19th centuries. Houses in or near the district may be old, and old houses often have slate or tin roofs, plaster walls, stone foundations and wiring that predates modern code.

The Commissioner of the Revenue's page lists a rehab tax credit for improving residential property in the Historic District. The real estate section at 540-372-1207 explains who qualifies.

The University of Mary Washington, Mary Washington Healthcare and GEICO are the major employers Wikipedia names for Fredericksburg, and tourism adds to the mix. About 1.5 million people visit the Fredericksburg area every year for the battlefield park, the downtown visitor center, museums and historic sites.

Many residents also commute by car, bus and rail to Washington, Richmond, and Fairfax, Prince William and Arlington counties. Most of the traffic heads north during peak hours on I-95 and U.S. 1, and the Route 1 bridge over the Rappahannock is often a bottleneck.

  • The University of Mary Washington, established in 1908 and opened in 1911, is a four-year public university inside the city.
  • Germanna Community College has a campus in the city.
  • The Virginia Railway Express and Amtrak serve commuters, and the FRED bus covers most of the area.

A landlord with a worn-out rental near the university or a commuter route sometimes decides to sell rather than renovate.

sections.h2: How does the weather affect houses in Fredericksburg?
sections.html:
Fredericksburg has a four-season humid subtropical climate with cool winters and hot, humid summers. Wikipedia's downtown climate table for 1991 to 2020 shows an average July high of 88.5 degrees, an average January low of 25.1 degrees, and about 43.4 inches of precipitation a year.

That mix puts steady stress on a house. Summer humidity feeds mold in basements and crawl spaces, winter freezes test pipes and masonry. An older roof can fail after a run of hot summers and wet storms.

  • Inspect the roof, gutters and flashing before listing.
  • Look for dampness along the foundation and in the lower walls.
  • Check older heating and cooling equipment, since failures often come at the worst time.

sections.h2: What are Fredericksburg's tax rate and due dates?
sections.html:
Fredericksburg bills real estate tax twice a year, with payments due December 5 and June 5. The Commissioner of the Revenue's page states that real estate is reassessed every four years and billed on a fiscal year that runs from July 1 through June 30.

The rate shown applies to the fiscal year that ended June 30, 2026, so check the city's Current Tax Rates page for the rate now in effect. The real estate office is at 715 Princess Anne Street, Room 107, and the number is 540-372-1207. The Treasurer notes that supplemental real estate bills can arrive on other dates in some cases.

sections.h2: What does a Fredericksburg seller pay at closing?
sections.html:
A Fredericksburg seller pays any real estate tax that is due, plus Virginia's grantor tax on the deed. Virginia law ranks the tax lien ahead of other liens, and the lien stays until the taxing authority is paid. The statute also states that the seller's tax liability is prorated by contract.

The grantor tax is 50 cents for each $500 of the sale price, and the seller pays unless the two sides agree otherwise. The clerk of court collects it when the deed is recorded, and the consideration must appear on the deed's first page.

  • Ask the Treasurer for the balance owed on the December 5 or June 5 installment.
  • Confirm that the 10 percent penalty has not been added.
  • Ask the title company to run a lien search before you sign.
  • Decide in the contract how the half-year tax will be split between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What problems do Fredericksburg sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here often hold an older house, a rental or an inherited property, and many are far from the city. Historic-age houses may need repairs a lender would insist on, and a house near I-95 or Route 1 can have noise issues that buyers push on.

A cash sale removes the repairs, showings and financing steps. We can buy directly or bring a vetted cash buyer, and any offer reflects the condition of the house and its title. Compare it with listing and with selling to a local investor, then choose.

faqs.q: When are Fredericksburg real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is due December 5 and June 5, or the next business day. The city adds a 10 percent penalty to balances left unpaid after those dates.

faqs.q: What is the real estate tax rate in Fredericksburg, VA?
faqs.a: For July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, the city lists $0.80 per $100 of assessed value, plus a fire tax equal to $0.01 per $100. Check the Current Tax Rates page for the newest rate.

faqs.q: How often does Fredericksburg reassess real estate?
faqs.a: The Commissioner of the Revenue says real estate is reassessed every four years. Call 540-372-1207 with questions about your assessment.

faqs.q: Is there a tax credit for fixing up a house in the Fredericksburg Historic District?
faqs.a: The city lists a rehab tax credit for improving residential property in the Historic District. Contact the Commissioner of the Revenue's real estate section at 540-372-1207 to learn who qualifies.

faqs.q: Who pays Virginia's grantor tax when a house sells?
faqs.a: The seller normally pays the grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the price, unless the contract moves it to the buyer. Your title company will show the amount at closing.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Fredericksburg rental or inherited house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer can purchase it in its current condition, with a tenant in place if needed. The title company still handles payoffs and the deed.
